title: Indonesian Tamarind Pork Satay Batches
seoTitle: Indonesian Tamarind Pork Satay Batches | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Satay skewer night—peanut glaze, coconut char, hall portions for ten
subtitle: Coconut-peanut glazed pork, cucumber pickle, and char for ten
description: Pork shoulder strips marinate in lemongrass and coconut milk, grill on skewers until caramelized, and finish with warm peanut sauce and quick cucumber pickle.

steps.title: Marinate pork strips
steps.instruction: Toss pork with coconut milk, lemongrass, turmeric, fish sauce, and brown sugar. Marinate at least 2 hours refrigerated. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use tamarind paste, galangal, coriander seeds, kecap manis as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Use Thai basil as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Quick pickle cucumbers
steps.instruction: Slice cucumbers thin. Toss with rice vinegar, pinch of sugar, and salt. Chill until service. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build peanut sauce
steps.instruction: Warm peanut butter with coconut milk, fish sauce, and sriracha until pourable. Hold at 140°F. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium-high, 425°F. Oil grates well. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Skewer and grill pork
steps.instruction: Thread pork strips on skewers. Grill 3–4 minutes per side, basting with peanut sauce, until charred and 145°F internal. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze finish
steps.instruction: Brush final coat of peanut sauce and grill 1 minute per side until sticky. Watch sugar—it burns above 450°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Rest skewers 3 minutes. Transfer to hotel pans, cover with foil, hold at 170°F. If tone drops, leave covered. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Serve with pickle
steps.instruction: Platter skewers with warm peanut sauce and cucumber pickle. About 8 oz pork per firefighter. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Cut pork strips uniform—thin ends burn while thick centers stay raw.
Pat excess marinade off before grilling to reduce flare-ups.
Peanut sauce thinned with warm coconut milk stays dippable on the line.
tonightSpread: Pork satay skewers with peanut sauce and cucumber pickle.
Steamed jasmine rice for a full plate.
leftovers: Pull pork off skewers for satay rice bowls.
Chop into lettuce cups with extra peanut sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Pork satay is a crowd pleaser that isn't pulled pork or sausage. Skewers glaze fast on a hot grill and hold covered at 170°F between tones.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate pork 2–8 hours. Grill medium-high 425°F. Hold glazed skewers covered at 170°F up to 35 minutes. Peanut sauce stays warm at 140°F on the line.
